body:
## Problem

Self-hosted runners under `.agent/tools/local-runner/` accumulate disk usage indefinitely under sustained job volume.

Two sources of growth:

- `runner-N/_work/<repo>` — every distinct repo a job touches gets its own persistent checkout. The runner doesn't garbage-collect cross-repo workspaces, so they accumulate one dir per repo that has ever run on the host.
- `runner-N/_diag` — diagnostic logs only rotate by date. The existing `cleanup-runner.sh` launchd job only deletes files older than 7 days, which can be too conservative on high-throughput hosts.

## Change

Wire `ACTIONS_RUNNER_HOOK_JOB_COMPLETED` (a built-in self-hosted runner feature) to a host-level cleanup script that runs after every job:

- **New `hooks/post-job-cleanup.sh`** — trims `_diag` to the last 30 files and drops anything older than 3 days; removes `_work/<repo>` checkouts not touched in the last 24h, skipping the current job's repo so checkout caching stays warm. Errors are swallowed so the hook never fails a job. Activity is logged to `runner-N/cleanup-hook.log`.
- **`setup-runners.sh`** — newly configured runners automatically get `ACTIONS_RUNNER_HOOK_JOB_COMPLETED` appended to their `.env`.
- **`README.md`** — documents the hook.

Existing runners need their `.env` updated and a restart to pick up the hook.

## Notes

- This is a self-hosted runner host-level feature, not a workflow change — workflow YAML is unaffected.
- The 24h / 3d / 30-file thresholds are defaults that can be tuned in the hook script per host.
title: Add post-job cleanup hook to self-hosted runner setup
